note: Prototype knowledge base. Chemical guidance is general label-rate information: always verify against the product label and your local agricultural extension officer before application.

apple_scab.summary: A fungal leaf and fruit disease common in cool, wet weather. Olive-green to dark brown velvety lesions form on leaves and fruit.
symptoms: Olive-green velvety spots on leaf undersides that darken over time
Distorted, curled leaves with scab lesions
Rough, corky scabs on young fruit
Early defoliation in severe infections
immediate_actions: Rake up and destroy fallen leaves at or after harvest
Prune infected twigs showing canker
Maintain proper tree spacing for airflow
prevention: Choose scab-resistant apple varieties where practical
Avoid overhead irrigation that keeps leaves wet
Apply protective fungicide sprays at bud break to petal fall in high-risk seasons

chemical_guidance.name: Mancozeb (75% WP)
chemical_guidance.note: Protective (contact) fungicide. Applied before or at first symptoms.

chemical_guidance.name: Captan
chemical_guidance.note: Verify local registration and pre-harvest interval.

organic.name: Sulfur spray
organic.detail: Wettable sulfur at 2-3 g/L during early season. Do not apply when temperature exceeds 30 C.

apple_scab.contact_advice: Contact your KVK or horticulture department for variety-specific spray schedules.

apple_healthy.summary: No disease symptoms detected. Continue standard orchard care and monitoring.
immediate_actions: Maintain regular scouting for early signs of scab or rust
Keep the orchard floor clean of fallen fruit
prevention: Prune for light penetration and airflow
Monitor weekly during wet seasons

maize_leaf_blight.summary: Cigar-shaped grey-green lesions that elongate along leaf veins, reducing photosynthesis and yields in humid conditions.
symptoms: Large, cigar-shaped lesions starting on lower leaves
Grey-green then tan-brown lesions along the midrib
Lesions merging and blighting leaf area in wet weather
Reduced grain fill on severely affected plants
immediate_actions: Remove and destroy heavily infested lower leaves early
Increase row spacing to reduce humidity in the canopy
Avoid late-season nitrogen excess that prolongs lush growth
prevention: Use tolerant hybrids where locally available
Crop rotation away from maize for 2 seasons
Deep-plough maize stubble after harvest to speed decomposition

chemical_guidance.name: Mancozeb (75% WP)
chemical_guidance.note: Contact protectant; good coverage of the canopy is essential.

chemical_guidance.name: Propiconazole (25% EC)
chemical_guidance.frequency: At lesion appearance, repeat after 14 days
chemical_guidance.note: Systemic; rotate chemistries to avoid resistance.

organic.name: Microbial biocontrol
organic.detail: Trichoderma-based products applied to soil/seed suppress leaf blight fungi. Follow product instructions.

maize_leaf_blight.contact_advice: Consult your local KVK for hybrid-specific management in high-rainfall districts.

maize_healthy.summary: No disease symptoms detected. Continue routine monitoring for leaf blight and stem borers.
immediate_actions: Continue weekly field scouting
Check for insect damage (stem borer) separately
prevention: Maintain balanced fertilisation
Remove volunteer maize plants between seasons

potato_early_blight.summary: Brown lesions with concentric dark rings ('target spots') on older leaves, favoured by warm, humid weather and nitrogen stress.
symptoms: Irregular brown spots with concentric ring patterns on older leaves
Leaf yellowing and death from the base upward
Dark, sunken lesions on stems
Fruit/tuber infection causing dry rot at harvest
immediate_actions: Remove and destroy the most affected lower leaves
Improve airflow with adequate hill spacing
Correct nitrogen nutrition if crops are weak
prevention: Rotate away from tomato, potato and other solanaceous crops
Use certified, healthy seed tubers
Avoid overhead irrigation in the evening

chemical_guidance.name: Mancozeb (75% WP)
chemical_guidance.note: Contact fungicide; timeliness and coverage are critical.

chemical_guidance.name: Chlorothalonil (75% WP)
chemical_guidance.note: Alternate with a systemic to reduce resistance.

chemical_guidance.name: Azoxystrobin (23% SC)
chemical_guidance.note: Systemic; use preventatively in wet conditions, limited applications per season.

organic.name: Neem oil spray
organic.detail: Mix 5 ml neem oil and 1 drop of mild soap per litre. Spray foliage every 5-7 days.

organic.name: Copper-based spray
organic.detail: Copper oxychloride at 2-3 g/L as a protectant. Follow label withholding period.

potato_early_blight.contact_advice: Get advice from KVK for district-specific fungicide rotation schedules.

potato_late_blight.summary: A destructive, fast-spreading blight in cool, wet weather. Water-soaked lesions, white fungal growth on leaf undersides, and rapid plant death.
symptoms: Water-soaked grey-green patches that turn brown quickly
White cottony growth around lesion edges on leaf undersides
Whole plants collapse within days in humid weather
Brown rot in tubers during storage
immediate_actions: Act the same day symptoms appear - late blight spreads overnight
Remove heavily infected foliage and dispose away from fields
Avoid working fields while foliage is wet
prevention: Plant certified disease-free seed tubers only
Apply protective fungicides before disease appears when blight weather is forecast
Destroy volunteer potato plants and cull piles

chemical_guidance.name: Mancozeb (75% WP)
chemical_guidance.frequency: Every 5-7 days in active blight weather
chemical_guidance.note: Protectant; must be on the plant before infection.

chemical_guidance.name: Metalaxyl + Mancozeb (68% WP)
chemical_guidance.frequency: At first sign; 2-3 sprays max per season
chemical_guidance.note: Systemic action for curative kick; strictly limit to avoid resistance.

organic.name: Copper oxychloride
organic.detail: 3 g/L as a protectant. Copper can suppress but not cure established blight.

potato_late_blight.contact_advice: Report suspected late blight to your KVK immediately - it is a notifiable crop disease in many states.

potato_healthy.summary: No disease symptoms detected. Maintain a good blight prevention schedule during wet weather.
immediate_actions: Keep scouting, especially after cool wet spells
Ensure plants are not water-stressed
prevention: Stick to the local blight forecast spray calendar
Use certified seed and rotate crops

tomato_early_blight.summary: Chlorotic lower leaves develop dark spots with concentric rings, leading to defoliation and sun-scorched fruit.
symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings on older leaves
Yellow halo around lesions
Defoliation starting at the base of the plant
Sunken leathery spots near the calyx of fruit
immediate_actions: Remove infected lower leaves and destroy them
Improve field ventilation and stake/train plants
Mulch soil to reduce spore splash from rain or irrigation
prevention: Rotate crops - avoid tomato after potato or pepper
Water at the base; keep foliage dry
Use disease-free transplants

chemical_guidance.name: Mancozeb (75% WP)
chemical_guidance.note: Contact fungicide; alternate with a systemic.

chemical_guidance.name: Chlorothalonil (75% WP)
chemical_guidance.note: Avoid applications within 3 days of harvest.

organic.name: Neem oil spray
organic.detail: Mix 5 ml neem oil with 1 litre water plus a drop of mild soap; spray every 3-4 days.

organic.name: Copper-soap mixture
organic.detail: Dissolve 2 g copper oxychloride per litre; apply early morning.

tomato_early_blight.contact_advice: Consult KVK for fungicide rotation guidance if the disease persists on multiple plants.

tomato_late_blight.summary: Rapidly spreading blight in cool wet weather. Large water-soaked lesions on leaves and stems with white mould on undersides.
symptoms: Large irregular water-soaked patches on leaves
White mould along the lesion edge on the underside of leaves
Dark firm lesions on stems
Fruit infection with wrinkled brown patches
immediate_actions: Act immediately - this disease spreads extremely fast
Remove and destroy infected plants and fruit
Do not work in wet foliage
prevention: Spray protectant fungicides before cool wet spells
Use resistant/tolerant varieties where available
Good staking and pruning for airflow

chemical_guidance.name: Mancozeb (75% WP)
chemical_guidance.note: Protective; coverage of lower leaf undersides is important.

organic.name: Copper oxychloride
organic.detail: 3 g/L as a protectant only; not effective once lesions are visible.

tomato_late_blight.contact_advice: Contact your KVK immediately - late blight can wipe out a crop within days.

tomato_healthy.summary: No disease symptoms detected. Keep up standard preventive practices during wet weather.
immediate_actions: Continue weekly scouting of lower leaves
Maintain staking and pruning
prevention: Water at the base of plants
Rotate crops and use disease-free seed
